entries.clue: Plight of conflicted Republican heads leading double lives (6)

indicatorNotes.heads: the heads of words are their first letters
indicatorNotes.double: double asks for the next piece twice

blocks.note: first letters of Conflicted and Republican
lives = IS (he lives = he is, he exists), taken twice

annotation.surface: A politician torn between parties is living two lives and finds himself in a fix.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lives' as 'is' is the hard step: to live is to exist, to be. 'Leading' only places CR in front.
annotation.definitionFit: A crisis is a plight, a time of serious trouble.

entries.clue: Excellent red for the diner? (4)

blocks.note: an old-fashioned sense of excellent, as in a fine old time
how a diner orders a steak that is still red inside

annotation.surface: A diner praises a fine red wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Red' suggests wine on a diner's table; it is the colour of undercooked meat.
annotation.definitionFit: Rare means unusually good, and rare meat is lightly cooked and red in the middle.

entries.clue: Somewhat over-tasked, add lead to make tracks (9)

indicatorNotes.Somewhat: only some of the words that follow are used

annotation.surface: An overworked person is asked to take on the lead role as well.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits the run of letters on the surface, but a hidden word ignores punctuation and runs across it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are informal ways of saying clear off in a hurry, SKEDADDLE being an American Civil War slang word.

entries.clue: Superior toys on high (6)

indicatorNotes.high: high as on drugs: the letters are out of their right minds

annotation.surface: Toys stored on a high shelf, out of reach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On high' reads as one phrase meaning 'up above'; 'on' is fodder and 'high' alone is the signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Superior and snooty both describe someone who looks down on others.

entries.clue: Pitiful account of boss turned politician (3,5)

indicatorNotes.turned: turned over, jumbled: the letters change places

blocks.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

annotation.surface: A news story about a boss who went into politics.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay splits the letters one place later than the enumeration does, so the politician hides across the word break.
annotation.definitionFit: A sob story is a tale of woe told to win sympathy.

entries.clue: White Cliffs of Dover composition – morris dance yet to be arranged by Kay (11,4)

indicatorNotes.to be arranged: arranging puts the letters in a new order

blocks.note: Kay is how the letter K is spelt out

annotation.surface: A new musical arrangement of the wartime song 'The White Cliffs of Dover', to be done as a morris dance.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics make the White Cliffs of Dover a song, so 'composition' looks musical; read literally, it is what the cliffs are made of. Morris dancing is English folk dancing.
annotation.definitionFit: The cliffs are chalk, a sedimentary rock laid down on an ancient seabed.

entries.clue: Wretched, mannered start of assault on Everest? (4,4)

annotation.surface: A miserable, stiff climber at the foot of Everest.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: an expedition's assault on the summit sets out from base camp.
annotation.definitionFit: Base camp is where a climb on Everest begins.

entries.clue: Not opening, force lock (5)

indicatorNotes.Not opening: without its opening, the first letter goes

annotation.surface: A door that won't open, so someone forces the lock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lock' is a lock of hair, not a door fitting.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once 'lock' is read as a curl of hair rather than a fastening.

entries.clue: The Pied Piper of abstract art – baseball player? (3-7)

indicatorNotes.abstract: abstract art distorts its subject, so the letters of ART are distorted

blocks.note: the catcher crouches behind home plate

annotation.surface: Someone is hailed as the Pied Piper of abstract art, a pied piper being a leader who draws a following.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abstract art' reads as a movement in painting, which hides that 'abstract' is working on ART.
annotation.definitionFit: The Pied Piper of Hamelin rid the town of rats by piping them away.

entries.clue: Sponge’s loose weight (8)

blocks.note: a load is a weight carried

annotation.surface: A bath sponge is light and floppy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' reads as a noun; here it is the verb, to live off others.
annotation.definitionFit: To sponge is to freeload, taking without paying your way.

entries.clue: Dick playing lute to break silence (6)

indicatorNotes.playing: playing with the letters moves them around
indicatorNotes.to break: the new letters break into the middle of SH

annotation.surface: A musician playing the lute breaks a hush.
annotation.walkthrough: S(LEUT)H. 'Dick' is old slang for a detective, as in private dick.
annotation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, and so is a dick in American slang.

entries.clue: Applying mascara isn’t a protection against greasy hair (12)

indicatorNotes.Applying: applying as in working on, putting to use: the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters, ignoring the apostrophe

annotation.surface: A beauty tip: mascara won't stop your hair from being greasy.
annotation.walkthrough: An antimacassar is a cloth over the back of a chair, named after Macassar oil, a Victorian hair oil it kept off the upholstery.
annotation.definitionFit: An antimacassar protects a chair back from greasy, oiled hair.

entries.clue: Intermittent sort of casino in Ohio state (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the anagram sits inside the state

blocks.note: O is an abbreviation for Ohio
CASINO rearranged, placed after the C of CAL

annotation.surface: An Ohio casino that is only open now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: Both abbreviations are old-style ones: O for Ohio and Cal. for California, rather than the two-letter postal codes OH and CA.
annotation.definitionFit: Occasional and intermittent both mean happening now and then.

entries.clue: Rocket salad starter with re-processed food (4)

indicatorNotes.starter: the starter of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: cud is food a cow brings back up to chew again

annotation.surface: A menu: rocket salad as a starter, then a dish of leftovers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rocket' is a salad leaf on the surface; the definition is the Scud missile. 'Starter' is a menu course too.
annotation.definitionFit: The Scud is a Soviet-designed ballistic missile, a rocket.

entries.clue: Never underestimate Middle Eastern leaders with lively ability to put two and two together (8)

annotation.definition: ability to put two and two together

indicatorNotes.leaders: the leaders of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Never, Underestimate, Middle, Eastern

annotation.surface: Advice not to underrate the shrewdness of Middle Eastern leaders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put two and two together' usually means working something out; taken literally it is adding, which is numeracy.
annotation.definitionFit: Numeracy is skill with numbers, such as adding two and two.

entries.clue: Just a blend of proper English and ordinary American (9)

blocks.note: O = ordinary, as in O level

annotation.surface: A remark on a way of speaking that mixes proper English with plain American.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blend' sounds like a call to mix letters, but the pieces go down in the order given. 'Just' is an adjective here, not 'only'.
annotation.definitionFit: Just and righteous both mean morally upright.

entries.clue: Uplifted, set sights on getting one around a scholarly environment (8)

indicatorNotes.Uplifted: lifted up: in a down clue the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ca. = circa, around, before a date

annotation.surface: An inspired person, feeling lifted, aims to join a scholarly setting.
annotation.walkthrough: AIMED + A + CA, then the whole lot is turned upward to read ACADEMIA.
annotation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholarship.

entries.clue: City’s very bitter new agents? (8)

blocks.note: bitter is a British type of beer, an ale
the CIA's agents, the US intelligence agency

annotation.surface: A spy story: the City of London is resentful of its new recruits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' reads as an adjective with 'very'; it is the noun, a British beer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Spain's third-largest city, on the Mediterranean coast and home of paella.

entries.clue: Team leader changed, became mature (4)

indicatorNotes.leader changed: the first letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: the C at the front becomes G

annotation.surface: A sports team got a new captain and grew up.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue does not say what the new letter is; the definition settles it as G.
annotation.definitionFit: To grow up is to mature, so 'grew' matches 'became mature'.

entries.clue: Was a fish factory worker disappointed? (6)

blocks.note: a fish factory worker guts fish
British slang for crushed, as if your insides had been ripped out

annotation.surface: Did the fish-plant worker feel let down?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' as bitterly disappointed is everyday British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone gutted is devastated, deeply disappointed.

entries.clue: A British duty to spread nudity (8,4)

annotation.surface: A patriotic call to spread naturism as a national duty.
annotation.walkthrough: The birthday suit is the skin you were born in.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the only suit you wear at birth is your bare skin, so the phrase stands for nudity.

entries.clue: Soil: it isn’t common (5)

blocks.note: ain't, the common or nonstandard form of isn't

annotation.surface: A gardener declares the soil isn't ordinary.
annotation.walkthrough: Say it as 't ain't, the country way of saying 'it isn't'. 'Soil' is the verb, to dirty.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with the verb sense of soil: to make dirty or contaminate.

entries.clue: In-house detective was a druggie (4)

indicatorNotes.In: the answer is found in the words that follow

annotation.surface: A hotel's own detective had a drug habit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In-house' reads as one word; split it, and 'In' is the pointer to letters inside 'house detective'.
annotation.definitionFit: To use is to take drugs, so a former druggie used.

entries.clue: Part of company that’s failing (6)

blocks.note: to be part of something is to be in it

annotation.surface: A division of a company that is going under.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Failing' suggests a business in trouble; here it is failing health.
annotation.definitionFit: Infirm means weak and failing in health.

entries.clue: Privy you once dumped in river? (8)

indicatorNotes.dumped in: one piece is dropped inside the other

blocks.note: the Ouse is an English river
thou is the old word for you

annotation.surface: A lavatory once thrown into a river, with a toilet-humour hint in 'dumped'.
annotation.walkthrough: OU(THOU)SE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name an old-fashioned toilet in a shed outside the main house.

entries.clue: Apartment charge for potential item of furniture? (8)

blocks.note: to charge is to load or pack, as you charge a gun

annotation.surface: The rent or fee for a flat, paid for a piece of furniture.
annotation.walkthrough: The furniture is only potential because a flatpack still has to be assembled.
annotation.definitionFit: A flatpack is furniture sold in pieces, waiting to be put together.

entries.clue: Dance figure is switched between two parties (2-2-2)

indicatorNotes.switched: switched round, its two letters change places
indicatorNotes.between: the piece goes between the other two

blocks.note: a do is a party, and there are two

annotation.surface: At a party, a dancer changes partners between two groups.
annotation.walkthrough: DO(SI)DO. The do-si-do is a square-dance move where partners circle back to back.
annotation.definitionFit: A do-si-do is a figure in square and country dancing.
